newsitem.title: BELGIUM: World steel output up four percent yr/yr in Feb.
newsitem.headline: World steel output up four percent yr/yr in Feb.

text.p: World crude steel production rose four percent to 59.1 million tonnes in February compared with the same month last year, boosted by better figures in western Europe and Asia, the International Iron and Steel Institute said on Thursday.

Production rose 4.6 percent in western Europe to 13.4 million tonnes. "In the Eurpean Union Germany and France continue to show higher production than in the same month last year, increasing by 9.9 percent and 15.4 percent respectively," IISI said in a statement.
However, British production was down 0.4 percent from the same month last year.
Eastern Europe's output fell by 3.3 percent to 2.3 million tonnes but production in the former Soviet Union rose 3.8 percent to 5.9 million tonnes.
North American output fell marginally, down 0.9 percent to 9.8 million tonnes while South America's production rose 1.6 percent to 2.8 million tonnes.
In Asia, steel production continued to show an upward trend, up by 6.9 percent to 22.3 million tonnes.
A total of 66 steel producing countries are included in the monthly data from IISI.
